title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch four-month outlooks issued 2019-2026 gave coral bleaching Alert probabilities about 3 times too high at 9-20 weeks ahead at 3,623 reef cells, but correct week-1 probabilities
abstract: Question: are the probabilities of the NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) Four-Month Coral Bleaching Heat Stress Outlook (v5, CFSv2 ensemble, 0.5 deg) reliable? Approach: a pre-registered verification of all 392 as-issued weekly outlooks from April 2019 to November 2026 against the CRW 5km satellite Bleaching Alert Area (7-day maximum) at reef pixels, 3,623 reef cells and 20 lead weeks. Because the outlook gives probabilities only in 10% bins, we use strict bounds: the observed count divided by the lowest (or highest) expectation that the bins permit. Result: at week 1 the Alert 1+ probabilities were correct (observed/lowest expectation 1.03, 95% interval 0.995-1.07). At weeks 9-20 the ratio was 0.32-0.35 (0.25-0.42), so Alert 1+ was given at least 2.9 times too often. Warning+ was at least 1.7 times too frequent; Watch+ was too rare. At weeks 5-20 the Alert 1+ probabilities had a worse Brier score than a cell climatology and an observed-state climatology. The excess acts like an additive floor: it was largest in the cool years 2020-2022 and in the Coral Triangle and Indian Ocean, and near zero in the Caribbean. Cell errors repeated between 2019-2022 and 2023-2026 (rank correlation 0.63). A lead-and-bin correction fitted on 2019-2022 removed the excess in 2023-2026 but only tied the climatology. The result holds for three truth definitions and in a back-filled 2011-2019 archive. Limitations: the truth is satellite heat stress, not observed bleaching; the suggested cause (a warm offset of model sea surface temperature against the satellite climatology) was not tested with model temperatures.

display.caption: Observed count of reef cell-weeks at each heat-stress level divided by the lowest (left) and highest (right) expectation that the 10% probability bins of the as-issued CRW outlook permit, for lead weeks 1-20, 2019-2026. Shaded: 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Left values below 1 mean too-high forecasts for any reading of the bins.

Weekly number of reef cells at Warning+ and Alert 1+: satellite observation (black) and the number expected by the outlook at leads of 1, 4 and 12 weeks. At 12 weeks the outlook expects hundreds of Alert cells every austral summer, also in 2020-2022 when few occurred.

Per reef cell log2(observed / forecast frequency) of Alert 1+ at lead weeks 5-12, 2019-2026. Red: forecast too high. The excess is largest in the Coral Triangle, Hawaii and French Polynesia, and small in the Caribbean.
